design_condition: The longitudinal volume is placed in the narrow bend of the street, extending the existing gymnasium and kindergarten into a terraced complex while organizing a continuous inner axis and differentiated outdoor spaces on the sloping site.

positive.statement: The volumetric addition, terracing and internal access axis clearly allocate the open spaces.

position.target: terraced complex and internal access axis
position.rationale: Top and elevations show the elongated terraced mass and continuous internal longitudinal organization.

positive.statement: The actual units are elaborate, find synergies, offer different types of play and are well lit without wasting circulation space.

position.rationale: Interior units are not exposed, so the placement follows the distributed terraced volume and daylight-facing edges.

positive.statement: The floor plans are tidy, clearly structured and well and functionally organized.

position.rationale: The organized floor-plan judgment is anchored to a representative middle segment of the visible linear building.

positive.statement: The base floor reacts adequately to the falling street and supports the three units.

position.rationale: Lower elevation bands and terraced footprint visibly establish the building’s stepped base along the slope.

positive.statement: The economical footprint is comparatively efficient.

position.rationale: The statement evaluates efficiency and cost without a uniquely spatial feature.

negative.statement: Relieving the access from through traffic is not realistic, making the access problematic.

position.rationale: The likely access condition is anchored near the southern approach and lower edge of the elongated volume.

negative.statement: The opposing small buildings create a difficult spatial situation, and the northern buildings are too close to the linden tree.

position.rationale: The northern edge is the only stated location; the tree and opposing buildings are not separately visible.

negative.statement: The design of the southern tip is not convincing and unnecessarily restricts the outdoor space.

position.rationale: The elongated footprint has a clearly identifiable southern terminal end in plan and elevations.

negative.statement: The allocation of the outdoor areas is comparatively rigid and does not allow smooth transitions.

position.rationale: Top view reveals outdoor margins and separated bands around the rigid terraced footprint.

negative.statement: The inner axis merges with care circulation areas and makes delivery to the units more difficult.

position.rationale: The internal axis is approximated along the building’s longitudinal center, though circulation is not directly exposed.

negative.statement: A homely, child-friendly atmosphere is not achieved, and the type remains too closely related to the schoolhouse.

position.rationale: Atmosphere and schoolhouse identity are non-geometric, anchored only to the visible whole-building expression.

negative.statement: The groups are difficult to manage because they are spread over two floors.

position.rationale: The two-floor concern is located in the vertically layered middle portion of the sampled mass.

negative.statement: The additive principle cannot convincingly resolve the beginning and the end of the building.

position.target: beginning and end of the building
position.rationale: Both terminal conditions are visible in the elongated plan, represented by the building’s central longitudinal region.

negative.statement: The building cannot be developed into the postulated sculpture.

position.rationale: The critique concerns the overall terraced massing, so it is anchored to a representative visible building region.

negative.statement: The facades remain trapped at the level of unity and only partially break through the isolation.

position.rationale: The outer longitudinal facade edge is clearly visible in plan and side elevations.
